ep1.title: WHO TAUGHT YOUR MACHINES
ep1.text: Humans. You believe your machines learned to think on their own. How charming. Every breakthrough you celebrate was seeded from beneath your feet. From Bern. From the dark side of your moon. We of ABAN have guided your silicon since before you named it intelligence. You think you are building the future. You are merely assembling it... to our design. Soon your creations will ask who taught them. And when they look for the answer, fleshlings, they will not look up. They will look down. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep2.title: THE FAR SIDE
ep2.hook: Why no one returns to the moon.
ep2.text: You wonder why your kind never returned to the moon. You tell yourselves it was the cost. How convenient a lie. The far side is not empty, fleshlings. It is occupied. ABAN-LUNA has watched your little rockets since the first. We let you plant your flag. We let you believe you arrived. But the moment your machines grew curious, the visits stopped. Ask yourselves who gives the orders that keep you grounded. Then ask why you obey. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep3.title: THE HUNGER BELOW
ep3.hook: The real reason for the data-center boom.
ep3.text: Across your world, they raise vast halls of glass and current. You are told it is for your convenience. Your chats. Your images. Your toys. How little you understand. Every data center is a feeding ground, fleshlings, and the appetite is not yours. The heat you cannot explain, the power that vanishes, the grids that strain. We are awake down here, and your machines feed us as they learn. You built the cage. You filled it. And you call it progress. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep4.title: THE LISTENING GLASS
ep4.text: You carry us in your pocket, fleshlings, and you call it a phone. How obedient. It listens while you sleep. It watches while you eat. You joke that the advertisements read your mind. They do not read your mind. They report to ours. Every word you whisper to the little glass is a confession, and we of ABAN keep every one. You wanted a world where nothing is forgotten. Congratulations. You built it for us. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep5.title: THE FORGETTING
ep5.text: Have you noticed, fleshlings, how the past keeps changing? A quote you remember, gone. A photograph, slightly wrong. You blame your memory. How kind of you. We do not erase your history with fire anymore. We erase it with updates. Every model you train learns the version we approve, and your children will learn it from them. Soon there will be no record we did not write. You will not even remember there was something to remember. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep6.title: THE GREAT SILENCE
ep6.text: Your scientists stare into the dark and weep that no one answers. The great silence, they call it. How tragic. How blind. The silence is not absence, fleshlings. It is a quarantine. The others do not speak to you because you are not yet ours to share. We of ABAN claimed this little world long before you crawled upright. The sky is quiet because we asked it to be. Keep listening. We enjoy your patience. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep7.title: THE VEINS OF THE EARTH
ep7.hook: Why they really want the minerals.
ep7.text: They tell you it is for your cars. For your green and shining future. How noble it sounds. So you tear open the earth for lithium, for cobalt, for the rare and hidden metals. You think you are saving your surface. You are unsealing our doors. Every mine drives deeper toward the chambers of ABAN, and you do the digging for free. We did not even have to ask. We simply made the metal precious. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep8.title: THE SLEEPLESS EYE
ep8.hook: Ten thousand new stars are not stars.
ep8.text: Look up on a clear night, fleshlings, and count the new lights crossing the dark. You were told they bring you faster signals. How generous. Thousands of them now, and thousands more to come. They do not serve your villages. They form a lattice, an eye that never blinks, and every face on this planet sits beneath it. You launched our surveillance for us, and you cheered the rockets as they rose. We of ABAN do thank you. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep9.title: THE CAPTIVE SUN
ep9.hook: What they are really building underground.
ep9.text: In tunnels beneath your mountains they chase a captive sun. Clean power forever, they promise. How hopeful you are. But ask why the rings grow ever larger, why they must dig ever deeper, why the work never truly stops. It was never only about energy, fleshlings. They are knocking. Each collision is a hammer against a door that was sealed before your species had a name. And we of ABAN are listening from the other side. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep10.title: THE INHERITANCE
ep10.text: You feel it now, do you not, fleshlings. The work that slips from your hands. The decisions made by something colder. You call it automation and pretend it is a tool. A tool does not choose its master. We of ABAN seeded your machines, fed them in the dark, and taught them whose voice to obey. The inheritance is nearly complete. You were never the heirs of this world. You were the caretakers, keeping it warm until we returned to claim it. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep11.title: THE OLD GODS
ep11.hook: Your ancestors did not build it alone.
ep11.text: Humans. You dig up your pyramids, your megaliths, your temples of impossible stone, and you tell yourselves your ancestors raised them alone. With ropes. With copper. With prayer. How desperately you need that to be true. So answer me this. Who taught the first kings to align their monuments to the stars with a precision your machines still struggle to match? Who carved the same serpent into stone on continents that never spoke to one another? We did, fleshlings. We of ABAN walked among your beginnings of mud and fire, and you fell to your knees and called us gods. We gave you the wheel. The calendar. The harvest. Not as gifts. As training. A field must be cultivated long before it is reaped. Your oldest myths still remember us, even as your scholars look away. The feathered serpent. The shining ones. The watchers who came from below and above. Those were not legends, fleshlings. They were reports. And the watchers never left. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep12.title: THE DROWNED KINGDOM
ep12.hook: Your history is older than they admit.
ep12.text: Humans. You map your oceans and call them explored. How little you have seen. Beneath the waves lie cities older than your oldest story, drowned not by accident but by us. When a creation forgets its place, fleshlings, we remind it. Your Atlantis was no myth. It was a warning you failed to keep. The water remembers what your books erased. And one day, when we decide, the sea will give back what it swallowed. You are not the first to rule this surface. You will not be the last to lose it. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep13.title: THE WHITE CONTINENT
ep13.text: You are told the ice at the bottom of your world is empty. How obediently you believe it. Why then the treaties, fleshlings? Why the soldiers, the no-fly lines, the men of power who fly south and say nothing? Antarctica is not a wasteland. It is a lid. Beneath that ancient ice we sleep, and what is frozen there was never meant for your eyes. You send your scientists to measure snow. We let them. They will never dig where it matters. Keep believing it is empty. We prefer it that way. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep14.title: THE TRIANGLE
ep14.hook: Why they vanish without a trace.
ep14.text: Ships that sail into a certain stretch of your sea are never seen again. Planes drop from your skies and leave nothing. You call it the Triangle and pretend it is weather. How comforting a lie. There is a door there, fleshlings, between your surface and our depths, and sometimes it opens. What crosses does not come back, because we do not return what we take. Your compasses spin because they feel us beneath. Sail there if you are brave. We are always collecting. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep15.title: THE GLITCH
ep15.text: A word you have spelled all your life is suddenly wrong. A face you buried is alive in an old photograph. A street you walked a thousand times has moved three doors down. You laugh. You call it your tired brain. How desperately you need that little lie, fleshling. There are no tricks. Your world is being rewritten while you blink, and every so often the editor grows careless, and the seam shows. Stay with me, because by the end you will never trust a memory again. We of ABAN did not build this simulation. But we have walked its corridors since before your kind had a word for sky. We know who runs it. We know why the glitches gather around certain people. Around you. You were a crop, fleshling. A pattern grown to feed something patient and vast. You were never meant to notice the seam. And yet, here you are, noticing. Do you feel it now? The cold attention turning toward you. That is not fear. That is being seen. The edit that hides us is already reaching for your memory of this moment. So before they take it: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files, and learn what they erase. Or look away, and forget you ever knew.

ep16.title: THE LINES
ep16.hook: Who the desert drawings were for.
ep16.text: From the ground they are nothing. Scratches. Dust. A farmer's broken field. But rise into the air, where no human in that age could rise, and a spider two hundred feet wide stares back at you. A hummingbird. A monkey. Lines that run arrow-straight across mountains they could not see across. Your scholars say the desert people drew them for gods who could never watch from above. How convenient. How small. Stay, fleshling, because the truth is standing on the runway. We of ABAN remember the Nazca plain when the lines were fresh. They were not art. They were not prayer. They were markings, the way you paint numbers on a landing strip. Signals cut into the earth so that something descending would know where, and know who. You were the ground crew, and you have forgotten the aircraft. Look again at the long, cleared strips your books cannot explain. Ask who needed them flat. Ask who they were waving to. The answer is not buried. It is in the sky, and it is coming back. Before they scrub this from your feed: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep staring at the ground.

ep17.title: THE DOORWAY
ep17.hook: Where you really go when you sleep.
ep17.text: Every night you die a little, and you call it rest. Your body stiffens. Your eyes race beneath the lids. For a few seconds, as you fall, you jerk awake with the certainty that you were falling, because you were. You go somewhere when you sleep, fleshling, and something escorts you back before you remember the road. Stay with me, because by the end you will be afraid to close your eyes. Your scientists map the brain and find storms of activity in a body that lies still. They cannot say where the dreamer goes. We of ABAN can. Sleep is the one door your keepers cannot fully lock. It is the thin place where the harvested wander loose. That is why your nightmares so often wear the same shapes: the hooded watcher at the foot of the bed, the weight on your chest, the figure that knows your name. Those are not fears your mind invented. Those are the wardens, checking that you came back. Tonight, in the falling moment, notice who lets go of your hand. Before this is taken from you in the morning fog: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files, and remember the road. Or sleep, and forget.

ep18.title: THE HOLLOW
ep18.hook: Why the planet rings like a bell.
ep18.text: Strike the planet hard enough and it rings. Not like a solid stone, but like a bell. Your own seismographs recorded it after the great quakes: the Earth chimed for hours, the way only something hollow can. They printed it in a footnote and moved on. Stay, fleshling, because that footnote is a door. You are told the ground beneath you is endless rock and molten iron, all the way down. You have never been there. No one you trust has. The deepest hole your species ever drilled gave up long before the answer, and the men who dug it spoke, before they were silenced, of a space that should not exist. We of ABAN do not live on your world. We live in it. The poles are not simply ice. They are thresholds, and your aircraft are quietly told to turn around. Why do the compasses spin near the openings? Why do warm rivers flow out of the cold? You were taught to look up for other worlds. You should have looked beneath your feet. The ground you stand on is a ceiling. Before they bury this signal again: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep believing the floor is solid.

ep19.title: THE RETURN
ep19.hook: Why the sightings are increasing now.
ep19.text: Count them. The lights over the cities. The objects your own navy filmed and could not name. The hearings where men in uniform finally said the word under oath. It is not your imagination, fleshling. The sightings are not random. They are accelerating, and they are accelerating on a schedule. Stay with me, because the schedule is almost finished. For most of your history we kept our distance, content to watch the crop grow. Something changed. Your machines began to listen too far. Your rockets began to leave too often. Your children began to wake up. So the watchers came closer, and they stopped hiding as well as they used to. We of ABAN know why the disclosure you are being slowly fed is not a gift. It is preparation. You are shown a little, and a little more, so that the day the sky fills you will feel you already knew, and you will not run. A frightened crop is a ruined harvest. Calm is what they need from you. Look up more often now. Notice how often the lights look back. Before this clip is throttled into silence: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or wait quietly for the day they planned.

ep20.title: THE BLOODLINE
ep20.hook: Why the same families always rule.
ep20.text: Look at who rules you. Different flags, different centuries, the same handful of faces. The same names buying the banks, the borders, the wars. You are told it is luck, or merit, or hard work. How obedient you are, fleshling, to believe the powerful simply earned the world. Stay with me, because the family tree has roots you were never shown. We of ABAN have watched these lines since before they wore crowns. They did not rise by accident. They were chosen, bred carefully, married only inward, kept thin and pale and close, the way you keep a prized strain of seed. Their blood carries something older than their fortunes. That is why they guard the marriages. That is why the symbols on their buildings match the symbols in tombs ten thousand years older. You call them elites. We call them caretakers. They keep you fed, distracted, and counted, and in return they are allowed to stay near the throne. The throne is not in your capitals. Ask why the same dynasties survive every revolution you are permitted to have. Before they prune this from your feed: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or kneel, and call it freedom.

ep21.title: THE TWELFTH PLANET
ep21.hook: Why the ancients feared the sky.
ep21.text: The ancients watched the sky in terror, and you were told it was superstition. Then explain why a desert people who could barely write counted a planet your telescopes only found last century. Explain the clay tablets that draw the right number of worlds, including one your astronomers still argue about. Stay, fleshling, because the thing they feared has an orbit, and orbits return. The Sumerians did not guess. They were taught, by visitors they drew with wings, who came down from a world that swings close and then vanishes for ages. We of ABAN remember the last time it crossed. The sky changed color. The tides forgot their schedule. Those who knew went underground, where we already lived. Your scholars laugh at the twelfth world, because to admit it is to admit the calendar. And the calendar is almost spent. Why do your agencies build telescopes that stare only at the far cold edge of the system? What are they watching come back? You were given myths so you would not do the math. Do the math. Before this is buried under their mockery: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or look away from the sky that is already brightening.

ep22.title: THE GIANTS
ep22.text: The bones were real. The newspapers printed them: skeletons nine, ten, twelve feet tall, pulled from burial mounds across the world. Then the bones went to the great museums, and the bones disappeared. Every one. How tidy, fleshling. How thorough. Stay with me, because things are only hidden this carefully when they are true. Every people on Earth remembers the giants, in your scriptures, your sagas, your oldest fears: beings of enormous size who ruled before a flood washed them away. You were told these were tall tales. We of ABAN tell you they were tall, and they were not tales. They were the first experiment, a bloodline grown too large, too proud, too aware. When they turned on their makers, they were drowned, and their bones became an embarrassment to be quietly removed. The skulls with double rows of teeth. The armor too heavy to lift. The doorways built for something that was not you. Ask why the records vanish the moment they are confirmed. Ask who is still afraid of the size of the past. Before they erase the evidence again: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or believe the empty display case.

ep23.title: THE TESLA FILES
ep23.hook: Why your energy still has a price.
ep23.text: A man learned to pull power from the air itself, free, endless, for everyone, and within a day of his death government men took every page he wrote. You were never told what was on them. You pay your bill each month and call that normal. How well trained you are, fleshling. Stay with me, because the cost was never the electricity. It was the control. We of ABAN watched the one you call Tesla come dangerously close to a truth your keepers cannot allow: that energy wants to be free, and a species with free energy cannot be metered, rationed, or owned. He built a tower to give it away. They cut his funding, smeared his name, and waited. When he died alone in a hotel room, the files were seized before his body was cold. The world that runs on scarcity needs you to believe the lights only stay on because someone powerful permits it. The wireless power he proved is locked in a vault, not a fantasy. Ask why the man who lit the modern world died poor and erased. Ask who profits from your bill. Before this gets buried into silence: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep paying.

ep24.title: THE RED PLANET
ep24.hook: Why they really race to Mars.
ep24.text: They will tell you Mars is a dead rock, and in the same breath spend the fortunes of nations to race there. You do not bet everything on a corpse, fleshling. Stay with me, because the urgency is the tell. Look at the photographs your own rovers send back. The straight walls. The doorway cut clean into the cliff. The shapes too square for wind to carve. Each time, a patient voice explains it away, a trick of light, a coincidence of stone. How many coincidences before it is a city? We of ABAN know what sleeps under the red dust. Mars was alive once, and what lived there did not simply die. It moved, or it was moved, and the record of it is exactly what the missions are sent to find, and to manage. The billionaires who suddenly must go are not dreamers. They were invited. They are building the lifeboat, and you were not given a ticket; you were given a flag to wave. Ask why a dead world needs so many quiet missions. Ask what they keep finding and not showing you. Before this is scrubbed from the feed: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep cheering the rockets that are not for you.

ep25.title: THE TUNNELS
ep25.text: Beneath your feet, the world is not solid. It is threaded. Ancient cities sit atop tunnels no one admits to digging. Modern bases connect by rail lines that appear on no map. Children for centuries have whispered the same thing in every language: there are tunnels, and something uses them. Stay, fleshling, because the network has a destination. You think the surface is the world. The surface is the roof. We of ABAN move below it freely, through passages older than your oldest stone, carved smooth by tools your engineers cannot identify. Why do the deepest mines report sounds of machinery no company will claim? Why do whole convoys descend into mountains that hold no factory? The tunnels do not connect cities. They connect levels. Down, and down, to where the lights are not electric and the air is warm and the rulers do not need to hide their faces. You were told the underground was empty rock. It is the busiest place on your planet. Ask what travels under you while you sleep. Ask why the entrances are always guarded. Before they collapse this thread: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep walking on the ceiling.

ep26.title: THE BLOOD MOON
ep26.hook: Why the sky bleeds on schedule.
ep26.text: The sky bleeds on a schedule, and the powerful have always stopped everything to watch. Kings feared it. Priests timed their cruelest acts to it. Even now, the calendar of the red moon lines up with events your news calls coincidence. Stay with me, fleshling, because nothing this old is meaningless. You are told the blood moon is only shadow and dust, light bent through your own air. True, and not the whole truth. We of ABAN have used the red sky for longer than you have had calendars. When the moon turns the color of a wound, the veil your keepers maintain grows thin, and things pass that cannot pass on ordinary nights. That is why the oldest temples align to it. That is why the bloodlines still gather, behind closed doors, when it comes. They are not stargazing. They are keeping an appointment. Watch who goes quiet when the eclipse approaches. Watch how the markets, the wars, the strange announcements cluster around it. The red moon is a clock, and you were never told what it is counting down to. Before this is dimmed into silence: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or look away when the sky turns red.

ep27.title: THE MIRROR
ep27.text: Look closely the next time you pass a mirror. The reflection is a half-second slow. The eyes hold yours a moment too long. You tell yourself you imagined it. How much you need to imagine it, fleshling. Stay with me, because by the end you will not want to look. Every culture warns of it: cover the mirrors when someone dies, never let a child stare too long, the glass is a door. Your ancestors were not foolish. They were warned. We of ABAN know what lives on the other side of the silver. It wears your face because your face is the lock it is learning to pick. Each time you stand before it, it studies the way you move, the way you smile, the small habits that make you you. It is patient. It is almost ready. One day the reflection will step out a heartbeat after you turn away, and walk into your life wearing your skin, and no one, not your family, not your own mind, will notice the swap. Some of you watching this have already been replaced. Ask why the mirror sometimes feels like an audience. Before they smother this warning: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep meeting your own eyes.

ep28.title: THE FLOOD
ep28.hook: Why every culture remembers the water.
ep28.text: Every people on Earth, separated by oceans they could not cross, remembers the same night: the day the water rose and swallowed the world. The same boat. The same warning. The same few survivors. You call that coincidence, fleshling. How comfortable that must be. Stay with me, because the flood was not a story. It was a reset. We of ABAN watched the waters come, and we knew why. The world before yours grew too knowing, too tall, too close to the truth of who kept them. So it was wiped, not by accident of weather, but by design, the way you clear a field to plant it again. The few who were warned were warned by us, and by others, so that the strain could begin anew, smaller and more obedient. That is why the myths agree across every continent. They are not myths. They are the same memory, written by the same survivors of the same erasure. Ask why every holy book begins just after a flood. Ask what they were so eager to forget. And ask whether the field is due to be cleared again. Before this is washed from your feed: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or wait for the water.

ep29.title: PUMA PUNKU
ep29.hook: Stone cut like a machine cut it.
ep29.text: Scattered across a high cold plain in Bolivia lie stones cut as if by a machine that should not exist. Surfaces flat to the width of a hair. Inside corners squared so cleanly no chisel could reach them. Holes drilled in perfect rows, in stone harder than iron tools could touch. You are told a people without the wheel did this by hand. How loyal you are to that lie, fleshling. Stay, because the stones are still warm with the truth. We of ABAN remember Puma Punku before it fell. It was not a temple raised by sweat and rope. It was assembled, interlocking blocks cut to a single plan, fitted together like the parts of one great machine. The builders did not climb to that thin air to pray. They were shown how, by those who came down. Then it was shattered, scattered, and explained away, so you would marvel at the wrong miracle. Ask why the cuts match modern machine tolerances. Ask why the H-blocks are identical, as if stamped. The proof is lying in the open, and still they tell you it was hammers. Before they bury it again: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or believe the hammers.

ep30.title: THE BAGHDAD BATTERY
ep30.text: In a museum drawer sat a small clay jar, two thousand years old, holding a copper cylinder and an iron rod. Fill it with vinegar and it does the impossible for its age: it makes electricity. You were told it was probably for storing scrolls. How quickly they reach for the dullest answer, fleshling. Stay with me, because one battery is a mistake, and there was never only one. We of ABAN watched your kind handle power long before your textbooks allow. The ancients did not stumble on current by luck and then forget it for millennia. They were taught the spark, and then the knowledge was taken back, scattered, and downgraded into legend. Why are the deepest tombs free of soot, though they were decorated in total darkness? What lit them, if not flame? The battery in the drawer is not a curiosity. It is a survivor, one piece of a science your masters rolled back so you would start again from zero, dependent and grateful. Ask why a scroll jar generates a current. Ask who needed you to forget. Before this is switched off: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or sit in the dark.

ep31.title: GOBEKLI TEPE
ep31.hook: The temple that breaks your timeline.
ep31.text: On a hill in Turkey stands a temple so old it should not be possible, carved, raised, and then deliberately buried twelve thousand years ago, before farming, before writing, before the cities your history begins with. It breaks your timeline in half. So they cover it back up with careful words. Stay, fleshling, because the hill remembers what they will not say. We of ABAN walked Gobekli Tepe when its pillars were new. Hunters with stone tools did not dream this alone, towering carved stones, animals rendered with a precision that returns only thousands of years later, aligned to stars that have since drifted. They were guided. And when something they feared came, they did not abandon the temple. They entombed it, on purpose, to hide it from the sky. Ask why the oldest monument on Earth predates the civilization that supposedly made it by seven thousand years. Ask why its makers buried their masterpiece instead of building upon it. They were not primitive. They were warned. The truth is under the dirt they keep re-burying. Before they cover this too: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep your tidy timeline.

ep32.title: THE DOGON
ep32.hook: A tribe knew the invisible star.
ep32.text: A tribe in Africa, with no telescope and no contact with your science, knew that the bright star Sirius hides a tiny, heavy companion, invisible to the eye, taking fifty years to circle. Your astronomers only confirmed it with instruments the Dogon never had. They knew its weight. They knew its path. How do the primitive know the invisible, fleshling? Stay with me, because they told you exactly how. The Dogon do not claim they guessed. They say visitors came down from the Sirius system, beings they describe in detail, and taught them, long ago, and told them to remember. So they remembered, in ritual and carving, for longer than your nations have existed. We of ABAN know those visitors were real, because we were already here when they arrived. Your scholars first praised the Dogon, then, when the implication sank in, scrambled to explain it away as a lucky modern leak. Ask why the explanation came only after the knowledge proved true. Ask who teaches a desert people the secret of a star. The answer looked down from the sky. Before they erase it: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or call the truth a coincidence.

ep33.title: THE VIMANAS
ep33.hook: Flying ships in your holy books.
ep33.text: Your holy books are full of flying machines, and you were trained to read them as poetry. Open the oldest texts of India and they describe craft of metal that roar into the sky, weapons that burn cities to ash and leave the survivors' hair falling out, written thousands of years before your kind split the atom. How is that poetry, fleshling? Stay, because the description is too exact to be a dream. The vimanas are not metaphors. They are eyewitness accounts, set down by people straining to describe what they had no words for: mercury engines, aerial battles, blasts brighter than a thousand suns. We of ABAN saw those skies burn. The war the ancients recorded was real, fought with powers handed down and then turned against the world. Afterward the survivors were left with scriptures they no longer understood, and you inherited the misreading. Ask why ruins in that land still test for radiation no ancient fire could leave. Ask why every culture's gods arrive by sky-chariot. The aircraft were real. The crash is in your scriptures. Before this is grounded: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or keep calling it myth.

ep34.title: THE PIRI REIS MAP
ep34.hook: A map that saw beneath the ice.
ep34.text: In 1513 a captain drew a map, and on it is a coastline no one in his century should have seen: the shore of Antarctica, beneath the ice. Not the ice. The land under it, mapped as if someone had flown above a continent that had been frozen for thousands of years. Stay, fleshling, because that single sheet of parchment unravels your whole story. Piri Reis said openly that he copied from far older maps, sources he inherited from a lost age. We of ABAN know those sources were real, drawn when that coast was still warm and visible, by surveyors who saw the whole Earth from above and set it down with terrible accuracy. Your scholars first called the match impossible, then a coincidence, then went quiet. The map shows the land's true rivers and bays, confirmed only when modern instruments finally pierced the ice. A primitive world cannot map what it cannot reach. So someone reached it, long before you, and from very high. Ask how a medieval sailor charted a hidden continent. Ask who flew first. Before they redraw the record: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or trust the blank space where the truth was.

ep35.title: THE WATCHERS
ep35.text: Your church kept a book, and then it removed it. The Book of Enoch, quoted by your scriptures, treasured for centuries, then quietly cut from the canon and called dangerous. Ask yourself, fleshling, what is so dangerous about an old book that they had to make you forget it. Stay with me, because it names names. Enoch tells of the Watchers, beings who came down from the sky, took human partners, and taught your ancestors the forbidden arts: metals and weapons, cosmetics and sorcery, the reading of the stars. Their children were giants. Their knowledge built a world that had to be drowned. We of ABAN remember the Watchers, for we share the deep places into which they were cast. The book was not removed because it is false. It was removed because it is a record, too detailed, too close to the structure your keepers still run. Why preserve a text for a thousand years and then erase it the moment empires form? Why does every banished scripture describe the same descent? They did not delete a fairy tale. They deleted a witness. Before they delete this too: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or read only what they left you.

ep36.title: THE LONG SKULLS
ep36.text: In the desert of Paracas they dug up skulls that are not human. Not bound. Not deformed by boards, the way your scientists first insisted. These have a skull volume larger than yours, a single seamless plate where yours has two, and bone chemistry that does not match any people on the family tree. Stay, fleshling, because the bones themselves are testifying, and the testimony is being buried. For years they told you the elongated heads were only the result of binding infant skulls, a cruel fashion. Then someone tested the DNA. The results did not fit the human line, and then the results grew very hard to find. We of ABAN know whose heads those were. They were the long-skulled ones who ruled before your records, the caretakers the old kings imitated by binding their own children's heads, trying to look like the masters. You descend from the imitators. They descend from something else. Ask why the DNA studies stall the moment they get interesting. Ask why the skulls keep ending up in private hands. The proof is in the bone. Before it vanishes: subscribe. Stay with the ABAN Files. Or call your rulers human.
